full_judgment:
2. Briefly, the facts of the case, are that the opposite party No. 1 as plaintiff instituted Other Class Suit No. 54 'of 2002, in the Court of Assistant Judge, Nagarpur, Tangail for rectification of the Kabinnama deed dated 14-8-1975 incorporating land of Schedule No. 3 in place of land of Schedule No. 2 of the plaint further case is that the land of Schedule No. 3 to the plaint measuring 115 decimals originally belonged to the plaintiff's husband Sukur Ali Mia. Sukur Ali Mia transferred the said land in favour of the plaintiff by a registered Kabinnama deed No. 19339 dated 14-8-75 for the purpose of dower money and maintenance and made over possession of the same in favour of her. Thereafter the plaintiff had been in the said land living with other family members by erecting homestead on 23 decimals of land in the Southern side out of 44 decimals appertaining to SA plot No. 294 under SA Khatian No. 104. The plaintiff has cultivated Irri paddy in the land of SA plot No 3/63 under SA Khatian No. 252. The plaintiff also cultivated Irri paddy and Master crops in 33 decimals out of 122 decimals appertaining to SA plot No. 2924 under SA Khatian No. 1010. 

 3. Further case of the plaintiff is that out of mistake 33 decimals of land appertaining to SA Plot No. 1948 under SA Khatian No. 1599 of Mamudnagar was written in the Kabinnama dated 14-8-75 as mentioned in schedule 1 to the plaint. Whereas Asaduzzaman, Kaful uddin, Abdul Hakim, Toazuddin and others were the owners of the said land and the said land was recorded in DP Khatian No. 80/1020/522/1645 in their names and the vendor of the said kabinnama deed Sukur Ali had no right, title and possession in the said land. The land of plot No. 2948 was under Khatian No. 1610 but inadvertently Khatian No. 1599 was written in the said Kabinnama deed. In fact in Khatian No. 1599 there is no land of plot No. 2948. The Kabinnama deed is required to be rectified by writing 23 decimals out of 44 decimals appertaining to SA Plot No. 294 under SA Khatian No. 104 in the said deed as mentioned in Schedule No. 3 to the plaint should striking out and 23 decimals out of 110 decimals appertaining to SA Plot No. 234 under SA Khatian No. 165 of Chamta Mouza written in the said deed out of mistake. The plot No. 234 under Khatian No. 72 belonged to Sundar Ali Sk and others which has been recorded in the names of Idris Ali in DP Khatian No. 87. Both Khatian Numbers and plot Numbers have been wrongly written in the said deed due to inadvertent mistake. In fact, Sukur Ali had title and possession in 23 decimals out of 44 decimals appertaining to SA Plot No. 294 under SA Khatian No. 104. It may be mentioned here that Sukur Ali transferred or gifted 105 decimals along with , chauchala structure standing thereon to his 1st wife by a registered deed of Heba billewaz No. 8065 dated 1-9-1975, moreover Sukur Ali during his life time transferred some land to his sons and daughters. The cause of action for filing the suit arose on 2nd Jaistha 1409 BS corresponding to 16-5-2002 AD when the defendants claimed the suit land and came to know that 2 pieces of land have not been incorporated in the deed dated 14-8-75 given by her husband and hence the suit for rectification of Kabinnama deed. 

 4. The defendant Nos. 1-4 contested the suit by filing joint written statement denying the material allegations of the plaint contending inter alia that there is no cause of action for filing the suit, the suit is barred by limitation; bad for defect of parties, barred by the provisions of section 42 of the Specific Relief Act and barred by the principles of estoppel under section 115 of the Evidence Act. The plaintiff had no title and possession in the suit land; 59 decimals of land appertaining to plot No. 3963 under Khatian No. 598 and 33 decimals of land out of 122 decimals appertaining to plot No. 2924 under Khatian No. 1610 of Mouza Mamudnagar and 23 decimals of land out of 43 decimals appertaining to plot No. 294 under Khatian No. 104 of Mouza Chamta along with other land were owned and possessed by late Sukur Ali and defendant Nos. 1 and 2 and land such was never transferred to the plaintiff by the said Sukur Ali by any deeds the Kabala deed dated 14-8-75 is out of forged and collusive deed The plaintiff never disclosed about the deed in question during the life time of Sukur Ali, who during his life time allotted his property among the heirs. During the allotment of property said Sukur Ali transferred 127 decimals of land in favour of the plaintiff and her sons born in her womb as claimed by them by a registered deed of Gift dated 19-4-1990 being No. 1992. Sukur Ali made over possession of the allotted share between the plaintiff and defendant by effecting partition separately i.e. by mets and bounds and in the circumstances if the deed in question is rectified this defendants will be deprived from getting their property and thereby shall suffer irreparable loss and injury and thus the suit is liable to be dismissed with cost. 

 11. 'The learned Advocate further submitted that both the Courts committed error of law in not considering that the suit is barred by limitation since the deed was executed on 148-1975 and during the BS Khatian the plaintiff recorded her name through her husband who executed the deed and the plaintiff also mutated her name'. The learned Advocate further submitted that in rectification of the deed section 31 of the Specific Relief Act should be strictly followed and since the petitioner did not file suit during the life time of the executant and the suit against the heirs of the executant cannot be maintained. In support he cited two decisions reported in 36 DLR 337 and 41 DLR 519. Thus he prayed for making the rule absolute. 

 15. On considering the evidence of the witnesses it appears that the parties obtained their respective shares which was made by Sukur Ali The plaintiff herself deposed in the court and stated that she mutated her name in the suit land. She also deposed that she obtained the deed from her husband and accordingly her name was property recorded in the BS Khatian. But on close reading of the evidence of the witnesses it is not clear that the said land was recorded in her name.
